clue.text: Live among troops in town in south Wales

indicators.note: among places the first word's letters inside the soldiers' word

parts.note: the artillery is the branch of an army that mans the big guns
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone makes their home with the soldiers garrisoned in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lodging with a garrison; 'Live' is really the verb to exist, and 'among' is the insertion signal. The place is a former coal-mining community in the Monmouthshire valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a former coal-mining community in the Ebbw Fach valley, Monmouthshire.

clue.text: Fundamental ingredient found by one in the deep

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter sits inside the word for the low voice

parts.note: the bass is the deep, low part in music
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A diver discovers the key component of something down in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deep' suggests the sea, but here it is the low register in music, BASS; 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the foundation or principal constituent of something, as in a sauce with a tomato one.

clue.text: Ski-slope in poor condition

definitions.meaning: a piste is a course that skiers descend, read here as two words
dilapidated or exhausted, usually written with a hyphen

explanation.surface: A piste that has been badly maintained.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description then synonym: a piste is a course taken to the bottom of a mountain, and something dilapidated is shabby.

clue.text: In fact in the act

parts.note: a deed is an act, something done

explanation.surface: Someone is caught truly red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are adverbs meaning truly or really.

clue.text: Reportedly exercises after being fortunate in the novel

indicators.note: after says the exercise sound comes behind the word for fortunate

parts.note: someone fortunate is lucky

indicators.note: reportedly asks for a word as it would be heard when spoken

parts.note: gym is school slang for physical exercises

explanation.surface: A character in a book is said to work out after a stroke of good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals a soundalike and 'after' the order. The book is Kingsley Amis's 1954 comedy about a hapless university lecturer, a staple of British reading lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the title of Kingsley Amis's 1954 comic book about a hapless lecturer.

clue.text: Again use c-celery recipe

indicators.note: a recipe is a set of instructions for mixing ingredients, so the stuttered vegetable's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A stammering cook brings out the same celery dish once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' is the anagram indicator, working on the seven letters of C-CELERY with its stuttered extra C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reprocess something so that it serves a second time.

clue.text: Measure designed to discourage further advances

definitions.text: Measure designed to discourage further advances

parts.words: Measure designed to discourage further advances
parts.note: advances here are loans of money, not romantic or military approaches, and the measure is a government restriction on lending

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a government policy restricting bank lending makes loans harder to obtain.

clue.text: Lady, by Jove, mistakenly found in the Balkans

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name, chosen because it comes from the Hebrew for princess or lady

indicators.note: mistakenly says the god's letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A woman is, to general astonishment, turned up in error somewhere in south-east Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Jove' reads as an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise, which hides the fact that 'mistakenly' is an anagram signal acting on the god's name alone, making JEVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina is a city located in that peninsula.

clue.text: Language that has cracked up is only partially intelligible

definitions.text: Language that has cracked up is only partially intelligible

parts.words: Language that has cracked up is only partially intelligible
parts.note: cracked up is taken literally as shattered, describing halting speech by a foreigner in the tongue of Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: halting, ungrammatical speech by a non-native speaker is hard to follow.

clue.text: Moving inshore he left substance used in making varnish

indicators.note: moving says the remaining letters shift into a new order
left says the two letters of the pronoun depart from the longer word

explanation.surface: A man relocating towards the coast abandons his varnish-making material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he left' takes HE out of INSHORE, leaving INSOR, and 'Moving' makes that into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this solid resin from pine trees is dissolved to make lacquers.

clue.text: Where to sit on board ship? …

definitions.text: Where to sit on board ship? …

parts.words: Where to sit on board ship? …
parts.note: on board suggests the floor of a vessel that passengers walk on, and a folding canvas seat is named after it

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the folding canvas seat was named for use by passengers on liners.

clue.text: … Exploration of a famous ship

definitions.meaning: the act of finding out about new lands
the vessel that took Captain Scott to the Antarctic in 1901, now berthed in Dundee

explanation.surface: Continuing the nautical theme, a voyage into the unknown aboard a celebrated vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym then example: finding new lands, and the vessel of Scott's 1901 Antarctic expedition.

clue.text: Many a foul faddist

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, which crosswords treat as many
rank means foul-smelling or offensive

explanation.surface: Plenty of people find a food obsessive unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an eccentric person with an obsessive enthusiasm.

clue.text: Sorting?

parts.note: to sort is to classify by kind, and a sort is also a printer's word for a piece of lettering, pointing to keyboard work

explanation.definitionFit: Punning synonym: classifying things by kind, with a nod to a printer's character.

clue.text: Inapt arrangement on TV container that is colourful

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, stacks the first part above the second
arrangement says the first word's letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the box is British slang for the television set

explanation.surface: An unsuitable display stands on top of a brightly coloured television cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints an ill-judged display on a television; 'arrangement' is the anagram signal making PAINT, 'on' stacks the parts in a down clue, and the TV is what Britons call the set in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tin holding an artist's blocks of pigment in many hues.

clue.text: Not quite score

parts.note: a score is twenty, so not quite a score is the number one short of it

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the number just one short of twenty.

clue.text: Boracic's transformation into another acid

indicators.note: transformation says the letters of the first word, including its final s, change into a new form

explanation.surface: A chemist converts one acid into a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformation' is the anagram indicator, and the possessive S of BORACIC'S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the acid known as vitamin C.

clue.text: Least sound?

parts.note: sound is noise rather than reliability, so the phrase describes whatever makes the smallest noise

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the one making the smallest amount of noise.

clue.text: The Yorkshire bird Harry followed found it was shaped like a wheel

indicators.note: followed says the name comes behind the other two parts

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is clipped to t'
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend
Hal is a pet form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman called Harry trails a bird and discovers it is circular.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern English dialect clips the definite article to a bare t', a convention crosswords borrow whenever Yorkshire is mentioned; 'followed' only fixes the order of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a zoological adjective meaning resembling a disc that turns on an axle.

clue.text: Jan and I do arrange to be in contact

indicators.note: arrange is an instruction to put the six letters of the three short words in a new order

explanation.surface: Two friends make plans to keep in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lie next to and touch something.

clue.text: Lose hope of the French duo

parts.note: des is French for of the, before a plural
a duo is a pair, two together

explanation.surface: People give up on a French double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to give up all expectation of a good outcome.

clue.text: Last month a couple of fellows had coffee

parts.note: Dec is how calendars write the twelfth and final month of the year
F abbreviates fellow, as in FRS, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Two chaps went out for a hot drink a few weeks ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last month' is not the one just gone but the final one of the year, DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an informal name for the drink with its caffeine removed.

clue.text: Height of poetic inspiration included in one's best rondeau

indicators.note: included in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A poet's finest verse shows them at the peak of their powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a literary word, from Italian, for a burst of creative fervour.

clue.text: Too many people, maidens perhaps, taking medicine

indicators.note: taking says the first part picks up the second beside it

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over, six balls, in which no runs are scored
a pill is a common form of medicine

explanation.surface: Excessive numbers, young women among them, are on medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maidens' are not young women but cricket OVERS in which no runs are scored; 'taking' adds PILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the surplus population that moves out of a crowded city.

clue.text: I had brought up schoolmaster, a Welshman

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, says the teacher's title is written upwards

parts.note: British pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: The speaker recalls raising a Welsh teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads as raising a child, but in a down clue it sends a word upwards; British pupils address a male teacher by the title used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a traditional Welsh male forename.

clue.text: Morbid fear that is beastly?

parts.note: beastly is taken literally, concerning beasts, rather than as horrid, so this is a dread of animals

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: an irrational dread of animals.

clue.text: A king and prince had the tapestry

parts.note: R abbreviates rex, Latin for king
ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince

explanation.surface: Two royals owned a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wall hanging named after the French town where such things were woven.

clue.text: German gateau?

parts.note: a chocolate and cherry cake is named after a wooded mountain region of south-west Germany

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the wooded region of Baden-Württemberg lends its name to a chocolate and cherry cake.
